verdicts.correction: (1) Subprogram L1C09V has a PROCEDURE DIVISION with no paragraph at all. That is not legal 1985 source: the ANSI X3.23-1985 procedure division format requires at least one section or paragraph ({paragraph-name. [sentence]...}...). A body with no procedure division statements at all arrives with ISO 1989:2002, the edition that states the implicit-GOBACK sentence §14.6.3 now carries. So the 85 golden depends on a construct 85 lacks. Fix: give L1C09V one empty paragraph ('       V1.' after PROCEDURE DIVISION). The sentence 'a procedure containing no statements acts as CONTINUE' still returns, and every expected line stays the same. The other option is to move the file to 2002. (2) The row's rule text includes the two fatal-EC-declarative sentences ('there is no next executable statement ... the run unit is terminated abnormally'). This golden does not pin them, so the row must not close on this golden alone. It needs the exit-code/stderr companion test the writer describes (the xfatal/xfatal2 recipe) before it counts as covered.

The program is not conforming source. 'INVOKE L1C09C "NEW" RETURNING S' breaks §14.9.23.3 SR3: 'The value of literal-1 shall be the name of a method defined in the factory interface of object-class-name-1'. L1C09C has no INHERITS clause and no FACTORY paragraph, so its factory interface has no NEW. In the standard, NEW is a method of the BASE class only (§16.2, §16.2.1), and no rule makes a class inherit BASE implicitly. A conforming compiler may reject this file, so the golden relies on a COBOL.NET extension. Fix: add 'CLASS BASE' to a REPOSITORY paragraph in class L1C09C, make its header 'CLASS-ID. L1C09C INHERITS FROM BASE.', and add BASE to the main program's REPOSITORY if needed. The expected .out lines ('M X=x K=2' / 'P X=x K=2') are correct and do not change. Existing goldens such as oo_hello share the same implicit-NEW pattern; that is a separate sweep.

Same program as GR-14.6.4-3, with the same defect: 'INVOKE L1C09C "NEW"' on a class with no INHERITS FROM BASE breaks §14.9.23.3 SR3, because NEW belongs to the factory interface of BASE only (§16.2.1). Fix: INHERITS FROM BASE plus CLASS BASE in the class REPOSITORY. The .out stays the same.

The program is not otherwise legal. The main program's 'INVOKE L1C09L "NEW" RETURNING S' breaks §14.9.23.3 SR3 on its own: L1C09L has no INHERITS FROM BASE, and its factory interface defines no NEW, only what its FACTORY paragraph declares, which is nothing. So a conforming compiler may reject the file for the INVOKE, not for §11.4.3 SR2, and the rejection does not isolate this rule. Fix: either delete the two INVOKE lines from L1C09Q (leaving STOP RUN), or add 'CLASS BASE' to L1C09L's REPOSITORY and 'INHERITS FROM BASE' to its CLASS-ID. The .err line is unchanged. Note that with BASE inherited the factory interface still has no SPEAK, so SR2 is still the violation.

all_upheld_flag: Not all upheld: 4 of 12 verdicts overturned. What I tried on each: I re-derived every .out from the code (C=5.00 -> 11.00 shown unsigned as 01100; ADD N N N TO N = 30+10 under §14.9.2.4 GR1; SORT/MERGE sequencing and section-range returns; item-identification order under §14.6.4 steps 2/3/4/5 before 7, checking §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 so the parenthesis after a function with no arguments is a reference modifier; the CALL GR3 e)/h)1 ON EXCEPTION path and the CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-72 rules for E1..E7). I ran cite.py --check on all 19 citations and all pass. I checked that each rule-breaking implementation would print something different (w/e instead of x/b; 80 instead of 40; missing IN-PROC/OUT lines). I checked edition placement: EC-EXTERNAL-FILE-MISMATCH is a 2023 EC name (VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE row 40), and no 1985 program can observe the 14.6.4-4 order. For each negative I checked that the rest of the program is legal: INVOKE SR3 on NEW, §9.3.8.2.3 rule 3 on PIC 9(4) vs 9(8). Main doubt: the 85-illegal empty PROCEDURE DIVISION finding rests on the 1985 format, which is not in the repo, so I derived it from the 1985 general format and the 2002 origin of the 'no procedure division statements' sentence. That is why it is overturned, per 'overturn when uncertain'. I did not check whether 85 defines falling off the end of a called program as an implicit EXIT PROGRAM, for the same reason.
